clue.text: Prince in favour of metal supports

blocks.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
tin is a metal
bras are supporting undergarments

explanation.surface: A royal who backs the use of metal props in building.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortinbras is the Norwegian prince who takes the throne at the end of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortinbras is a character in Shakespeare's Hamlet, the crown prince of Norway.

clue.text: Female provided note from flute

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
provided that means if
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A woman draws a particular note out of her flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small, high-pitched flute played in military bands, so it is a kind of flute.

clue.text: Rex Mason's terribly extortionate prices

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: Rex, Latin for king, is abbreviated R
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man called Rex Mason is charging outrageous sums.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a first name, but it is the king's R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransoms are sums demanded under threat, which makes them the most extortionate of prices.

clue.text: Fat? Felt anxious, worried, uncertain about what should be done?

definitions.text: uncertain about what should be done

indicators.note: worried can mean tugged about and shaken, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called fat feels anxious and fretful, unsure what to do next.
explanation.walkthrough: The anxiety in the surface spills over to make worried look like more of the same feeling; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Flux is constant change, so someone in that condition has nothing settled and cannot decide on a course.

clue.text: One serving Arthur during drinking spree

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a bender is a drinking bout
Art is the short form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: Someone pours drinks for a man named Arthur while he is out on a binge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender is the person who serves drinks behind a bar.

clue.text: Drink containing very soft fruit

indicators.note: a drink containing something holds it inside, so the other piece goes within

blocks.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A beverage with pieces of overripe fruit floating in it.
explanation.walkthrough: pp stands for pianissimo, the musical direction for very quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common tree fruit, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Items stolen from son, habitual joker

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
a wag is a person who is always making jokes

explanation.surface: Loot taken from a boy who is forever playing pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for a burglar's loot, the goods taken in a theft.

clue.text: Punishment? Why?

blocks.note: first meaning: to give someone a severe scolding or beating
second meaning: a question asking the purpose of something

explanation.surface: Someone being punished protests and asks the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone what for is an informal idiom for punishing or scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an idiom for a harsh telling-off and a plain question asking for a reason.

clue.text: Good landlord's blue tale

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a host is a landlord of an inn, with the possessive s kept
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A pub landlord tells a racy or a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue looks like it means smutty or sad, but it is the UK Conservative party colour; a Tory is a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost story is a kind of tale, one about spirits and hauntings.

clue.text: Selfish remark from one fairly good sailor after start of manoeuvres

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the opening letter of manoeuvres
all right means satisfactory, fairly good
Jack, or Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A decent sailor, out on exercises, says something self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for the attitude of someone who is comfortable and cares nothing for others. 'After' places the sailor and his rating behind the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said by a person content with their own lot and indifferent to others, so it is a typically selfish comment.

clue.text: Loud, and not just in pleasure ground

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
not just means unjust, unfair

explanation.surface: Noisy and unjust goings-on at an amusement park.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is an outdoor fair of rides and sideshows, a ground set aside for pleasure and amusement.

clue.text: Fish in European river - member gets a small number

blocks.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written
No. is the short form of number, small meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in a European river, and an MP catches a few of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Fish in' reads as a fish in the river; 'in' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompano is a food fish of warm Atlantic waters, related to the jacks.

clue.text: Uncomfortably hot, I tell her off on a whim

indicators.note: something sitting uncomfortably is out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling the heat, someone scolds a woman for no real reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing something just for fun with no reason, which is acting on a passing impulse.

clue.text: Lout, old criminal, bundled into helicopter

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, so the letters of the preceding word are bent out of order
being bundled into a vehicle puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: chopper is the informal word for a helicopter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aged crook is shoved into a helicopter by a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: Criminal reads as a noun with old describing him, but it is the signal to rearrange old.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, boorish person, so a lout is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Record broken by unknown composer

indicators.note: a thing broken by something has that something wedged into the gap

blocks.note: to list something is to record it
in algebra unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A record smashed by a composer nobody has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: Record looks like a disc that gets broken, but here it is the verb list.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Soldier and sailor back on leave

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to desert is to leave
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A soldier and a sailor return home on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the turned sailor after the leave word. Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the British 7th Armoured Division, which fought in the North African desert.

clue.text: Firm dates fixed quickly

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: An organisation sets its appointment dates in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company setting dates; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolutely unwavering, which is a sense of firm as an adjective.

clue.text: Duke is vulgar, reportedly, in speech

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said by others, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written
coarse means vulgar, and course is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A duke is rumoured to use crude language when he talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal spoken or written treatment of a subject, so it is a speech.

clue.text: Rest brood, depressed

blocks.note: a hen sits on eggs to brood them
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Take a break, mope, feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Brood suggests moody thought, but here it is the hen's sitting on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit down is to take a seat and so to rest.

clue.text: Fish cigarette out of front of sideboard

indicators.note: out of here means taken away from, so a letter is removed
the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette
the opening letter of sideboard

explanation.surface: A smoker keeps a cigarette by the fish on the sideboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A gasper is dated British slang for a cigarette; drop its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The gaper is a name for a sea fish, the comber, so called for its wide mouth.

clue.text: Settler, one taking part in landing

indicators.note: taking part in something means being inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a pier is a landing stage for boats
taken as written

explanation.surface: A colonist joins in the first landing on new shores.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first to settle a new territory, so an early settler.

clue.text: Released from nick in an unfit physical state

blocks.note: released from somewhere means out of it
nick is British slang for condition, as in good nick

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed from jail is in poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as slang for prison, but it is the other British sense, condition, as in a car in good nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of condition is the idiom for being unfit and lacking stamina.

clue.text: Eclipse abroad to study

blocks.note: abroad can mean out and about
to do a subject is to study it, as in doing history

explanation.surface: Go overseas to get ahead in study.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to surpass them, which is what outdo means.

clue.text: District of Colombia realtor

indicators.note: of means taken from, so the letters come from within the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: An estate agent covering a part of Colombia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes District of Columbia, but the spelling is the country Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: Work issue

blocks.note: first meaning: something produced by effort
second meaning: a result or outcome

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare nouns that read like a workplace problem are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is a piece of work made, and also the result or outcome that issues from something.

clue.text: Unpaid, a wretched RU team

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, broken state, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miserable rugby union side whose players get no money.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part in a sport without pay, unlike a professional.

clue.text: Call from Trier in Germany

indicators.note: from means drawn out of, so the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words
surface padding: places Trier, a German city, and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A phone call made from the German city of Trier.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British usage for phoning them, so a ring is a call.

clue.text: Eliminate king in another foreign country

indicators.note: foreign means strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are made strange by rearranging
in here means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: KO, a knockout, eliminates a boxer
R, from rex, is king
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to remove a monarch in some other overseas state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign country' reads as one phrase, but foreign is the signal to rearrange another; KO is knock out, a knockout eliminating a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is a state in East Asia, so it is an example of a country.
